deep.reconstruction:
The page has two strands: (A) building and analysing an explicit degree-7 rational map of the sphere, and (B) rewriting Laplace's equation in spherical coordinates using stereographic coordinates η, η' (η' is the conjugate). Together with the previous page, which also uses y, y', s, cubes and (s²−1/s²) dlog s, this matches the setting of Riemann's minimal-surface work, where η = tan(θ/2)e^{iφ} is the stereographic coordinate of the normal. That context is my inference, not stated on the page.

(A1) Ansatz. Riemann sets y = η³(η⁴+β)/(βη⁴+1) and writes
y − 1 = (η⁷ + βη³ − βη⁴ − 1)/(βη⁴+1).
He asks that η = 1 be a triple zero of the numerator N(η). He differentiates:
- N'(η) = 7η⁶ + 3βη² − 4βη³. At η = 1 this is 7 − β, so β = 7.
- N'' is written as 6·7η⁵ + 6βη² − 2·6βη. The correct N'' is 42η⁵ + 6βη − 12βη²; the two β-terms have their powers swapped, but the value at η = 1 (42 − 6β) is the same. It vanishes for β = 7.
So he fixes y = η³(η⁴+7)/(7η⁴+1), written twice on the page.

My additions (ramification). The map has degree 7.
- y ~ η³ at η = 0 and y ~ η³/7 at η = ∞: local degree 3 at each.
- y(±1) = ±1 and y(±i) = ∓i, each with local degree 3.
- So all ramification lies over the six octahedron vertices 0, ∞, ±1, ±i. The total, 2+2+4·2 = 12 = 2·7 − 2, matches Riemann–Hurwitz.
- The map is equivariant: y(iη) = −i·y(η), y(1/η) = 1/y(η), and y(−1/η) = −1/y(η) (commutes with the antipodal map).
The figure (a sphere cut by arcs into cells, with points marked i, ∘, ×, ∞) is apparently the cell decomposition / sheet structure of this covering.

(A2) Differential (right column). Riemann's first two lines carry the denominator (7η⁴+1) unsquared; the last line is correct:
dy = [(7η⁴+1)(7η⁶+21η²) − (η⁷+7η³)·28η³]/(7η⁴+1)² dη
= 7η² dη [(7η⁴+1)(η⁴+3) − (η⁴+7)·4η⁴]/(7η⁴+1)²
= 7η² dη (3η⁸ − 6η⁴ + 3)/(7η⁴+1)²
= 21η² (η⁴−1)²/(7η⁴+1)² dη.
This confirms the critical points η = 0, ∞ and η⁴ = 1.

(B) Laplace equation. He writes the spherical Laplacian
∂(sinθ ∂U/∂θ)/(sinθ ∂θ) + ∂²U/(sin²θ ∂φ²) + ∂(r² ∂U/∂r)/∂r.
Multiplying by sin²θ, and using s = log tan(θ/2) (so sinθ ∂/∂θ = ∂/∂s) and l = log r, he gets
sin²θ (U_ll + U_l) + U_ss + U_φφ = 0.
With log η = s + iφ and log η' = s − iφ:
- 2iφ = log η − log η' and 2s = log η + log η'.
- ∂U/∂log η = ½ ∂U/∂s − (i/2) ∂U/∂φ.
- U_ss + U_φφ = 4 ∂²U/∂log η ∂log η'.
- sin θ = 2tan(θ/2)/(1+tan²(θ/2)), so sin²θ = 4ηη'/(1+ηη')².
Result:
4 ∂²U/∂log η ∂log η' + 4ηη'/(1+ηη')² (∂²U/∂log r² + ∂U/∂log r) = 0.
He notes the Cartesian coordinates:
- z = r(1−ηη')/(1+ηη'),
- r·η/(1+ηη') and r·η'/(1+ηη') for x ± iy, each up to a factor 2 that he omits.

(A3) Product. Riemann expands
(7η'⁴+1)(7η⁴+1)(1+yy')
= 49η⁴η'⁴ + 7(η⁴+η'⁴) + 1 + η⁷η'⁷ + 7η³η'³(η⁴+η'⁴) + 49η³η'³.
Put p = ηη', q = η/η', u = q² + q⁻² (my notation). Then η⁴+η'⁴ = p²u, and the expression is the palindromic septic
p⁷ + 7u p⁵ + 49p⁴ + 49p³ + 7u p² + 1.
The factor 1+ηη' splits off; this reflects the antipodal equivariance. A first attempt is struck out. He then gets
(p+1) p³ [p³+p⁻³ − (p²+p⁻²) + (p+p⁻¹)(1+7u) + 48 − 7u].
With t = p + 1/p (my naming of his t) the bracket becomes his cubic
t³ − t² + t(−2 + 7u) + (1 − 7q²)(1 − 7q⁻²),
since the constant 50 − 7u equals (1−7q²)(1−7q⁻²).
The evident purpose: 1 + y(η)·y(η)' = 0 describes pairs whose images are antipodal on the y-sphere (with y' read as the image of the second point η'). The factor 1+ηη' gives the trivial solution (antipodal η'); the cubic in t describes the other solutions.
errors: In the first two lines of dy the denominator is written (7η⁴+1) instead of (7η⁴+1)²; the final line has the square, so this is a transcription slip with no consequence.
The second derivative of N(η) is written 6·7η⁵ + 6βη² − 2·6βη; correctly it is 42η⁵ + 6βη − 12βη². The value at η = 1 (42 − 6β) is unaffected, so β = 7 stands.
The Cartesian coordinates r·η/(1+ηη') and r·η'/(1+ηη') omit the factor 2 (x+iy = 2rη/(1+ηη')); the factor 2tan(θ/2)/(1+tan²(θ/2)) is written just above, so this is shorthand.
Everything else checks: the derivative, the η,η' form of the Laplacian, the factorisation by (1+ηη'), and the cubic in t.

results.what: Explicit degree-7 rational map y = η³(η⁴+7)/(7η⁴+1), with β fixed by requiring a triple point at η = 1. Its ramification lies exactly over the octahedron vertices (each of the 6 critical points has local degree 3), and it is equivariant under η→iη, η→1/η and the antipodal map.
results.modern_name: Rational function with prescribed branching / branched covering of the sphere with octahedral branch data (Belyi-type / Schwarz–Klein polyhedral maps)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (existence theory, 1857); explicit polyhedral rational functions are associated with Schwarz (1873) and Klein (1875–1884)

results.what: Laplace equation in spherical coordinates rewritten with stereographic variables: 4 U_{logη logη'} + 4ηη'/(1+ηη')² (U_{log r log r} + U_{log r}) = 0
results.modern_name: Laplacian in spherical coordinates, conformal (stereographic / Mercator) form
results.usually_credited_to: standard (Laplace, Gauss; conformal coordinates classical by 1850s)

results.what: Factorisation of (7η⁴+1)(7η'⁴+1)(1+yy') as (1+ηη')(ηη')³ times a cubic in t = ηη' + 1/(ηη') with coefficients in (η/η')²
results.modern_name: antipodal-equivariance / symmetric reduction of a palindromic polynomial

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit construction of a rational map with ramification over the octahedral vertices, together with its symmetry analysis, anticipates the explicit polyhedral functions of Schwarz and Klein (1870s). It fits Riemann's own branched-covering ideas and his minimal-surface work (η as stereographic normal coordinate), so it is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major priority shift. The Laplacian manipulation is routine.

checkable.asserts: β = 7 makes η = 1 a triple zero of y − 1
